pysnap.core package¶

Core business logic package for PySnap.

Submodules¶

pysnap.core.access module¶

How PySnap reaches the guest of a VM: serial console or ssh.

Base VMs registered with pysnap protosettings and their clones are known to have their console on COM1, so they are reached through the serial TCP server of COM1. Every other VM is reached through ssh: its NAT adapter forwards a host port on 127.0.0.1 to port 22 of the guest. The automatic choice can be overridden per VM with pysnap set VM access=com|ssh.

The override and the ssh user are kept in VirtualBox extra data of the VM; the forwarded port is read from the NAT port-forwarding rule named SSH_RULE_NAME.

run_integration_test(image_path, name_token=None)[source]¶

Run an end-to-end integration scenario on an appliance.

The scenario imports one appliance VM, creates three linked clones connected in a triangle of internal networks, captures machine details, validates runtime monitoring by attaching to one clone and starting a second clone headlessly, and removes all created VMs one by one.

Parameters:

  • image_path (str) – Path to the appliance used for the test.

  • name_token (str | None) – Optional deterministic suffix for generated VM names.

Returns:

Integration test result with machine info and deletion order.

Raises:

PySnapError – If the appliance is invalid or the test fails.

Return type:

IntegrationTestResult

plug_vm(vm_name)[source]¶

Configure one VM for PySnap connections.

A VM reached through COM1 gets UART1 as a TCP server: if it already is one, the VM is returned unchanged; otherwise PySnap assigns a free TCP port and enables the same UART1 tcpserver mode used by the imported protocol images. A VM reached through ssh gets a NAT rule that forwards a free host port to port 22 of the guest.

Parameters:

vm_name (str) – VM name to configure.

Returns:

Updated VM information.

Raises:

PySnapError – If the VM cannot be configured safely.

Return type:

VMInfo

set_vm_settings(vm_name, options)[source]¶

Change the serial ports and network adapters of a stopped VM.

Without options the current settings are returned unchanged. All options are validated before one modifyvm call applies them. For proto-settings clones the DMI system SKU is rebuilt from the new COM1 port and the internal networks of NIC2-NIC4.

Parameters:

  • vm_name (str) – VM name.

  • options (Sequence[str]) – comN=VALUE and nicN=VALUE options.

Returns:

Settings after the change and warnings.

Raises:

PySnapError – For invalid options, a VM that is not stopped or TCP ports in use.

Return type:

VMSettingsResult

prepare_ssh_terminal(vm_name, *, timeout=None, notify=None, installer=None, poll_interval=2.0)[source]¶

Wait for the guest ssh server and make sure the PySnap key works.

A freshly started guest needs time to boot, so a missing ssh server is retried until timeout. A refused key starts the interactive key setup of setup_ssh_key() in the current terminal.

Parameters:

  • vm_name (str) – Name of a running VM reached through ssh.

  • timeout (float | None) – Seconds to wait for the ssh server.

  • notify (Callable[[str], None] | None) – Callback for progress messages.

  • installer – Interactive installer, for tests.

  • poll_interval (float) – Seconds between attempts.

Returns:

Connection target for the ssh user of the VM.

Raises:

PySnapError – When no ssh server answers in time or the key cannot be installed.

Return type:

SshTarget

setup_ssh_key(vm_name, user=None, *, console=False, installer=None, console_wait=10.0)[source]¶

Install the PySnap key in the guest so that ssh needs no password.

By default ssh logs in with the password of user (the ssh user of the VM) in the current terminal, adds the key for that user and, when the root password is given in the guest, for root as well. With console the key line is typed on the VM screen instead, for a shell that is logged in there. When the ssh user of the VM cannot use the key but user can, the ssh user is switched to user.

Parameters:

  • vm_name (str) – VM name.

  • user (str | None) – Guest user for the password login.

  • console (bool) – Type the command on the VM screen.

  • installer – Interactive installer, for tests.

  • console_wait (float) – Seconds to wait for a typed command to work.

Returns:

Users that can log in with the key afterwards.

Raises:

PySnapError – When no ssh server answers or nothing worked.

Return type:

SshKeyResult

pysnap.core.settings module¶

Parse pysnap set options for serial ports and network adapters.

Each option is KEY=VALUE:

  • comN: auto or a TCP port number for a TCP server, server:NAME or client:NAME for a host pipe between VMs, or off;

  • nicN: an internal network name, nat or off;

  • access: com, ssh or auto (the choice by protosettings);

  • ssh-user: the guest user for ssh connections.

N is any port or adapter number; whether the VM has it (VirtualBox offers COM1-COM4 and, depending on the chipset, NIC1-NIC8 or NIC1-NIC36) is checked against the VM.

A host pipe is given by a short name; host_pipe_path() turns it into the path format of the host system, so two VMs that use the same name are connected on any platform.
